# The chain of agents crosses processes over MCP too (D2): Outer calls Inner, which runs in
# another process (`metagente serve --stdio`), and Inner calls Outer back, in a third. The
# third process is told that Outer is already running, and refuses.
#
# A tool server never receives a variable of Metagente, so the processes find the approvals where
# a real installation keeps them: in the configuration folder of the user, outside the project.
env METAGENTE_CONFIG_DIR=
env HOME=$WORK/home
env USERPROFILE=$WORK/home
env APPDATA=$WORK/home/appdata
env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$WORK/home/.config
mkdir $WORK/home
cd project

exec metagente trust --yes outer.ag
exec metagente trust --yes inner.ag

# One hop works, and Inner knows who called.
exec metagente run outer.ag hello
stdout '^Inner was called$'

# The circle is stopped, and says so.
! exec metagente run outer.ag loop
stderr 'calling each other in a circle'

-- project/outer.ag --
agent Outer
  goal "Call Inner, and be called back by it"
  tool inner from mcp "metagente serve inner.ag --stdio"
  accepts hello
  accepts loop
  accepts ping
  on hello
    reply inner.Inner__hello
  on loop
    reply inner.Inner__back
  on ping
    reply "pong"
-- project/inner.ag --
agent Inner
  goal "Answer, or call Outer back"
  tool outer from mcp "metagente serve outer.ag --stdio"
  accepts hello
  accepts back
  on hello
    reply "Inner was called"
  on back
    reply outer.Outer__ping
